'''White Plains''' is a city in and the [[county seat]] of [[Westchester County, New York]], United States. It is <!--- the 28th-largest municipality in the state of New York, --->an [[inner suburb]] of [[New York City]], and a commercial hub of Westchester County, a densely populated suburban county that is home to about one million people. White Plains is located in south-central Westchester County. Its downtown (Mamaroneck Avenue) is {{convert|25|mi}} north of [[Midtown Manhattan]].

The city's total population was 59,599 in the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]],<ref>United States Census Bureau, 2020 Report, White Plains, New York</ref> up from 53,077 at the 2010 census.<ref name="Census 2010">{{Cite web |title=Geographic Identifiers: 2010 Demographic Profile Data (G001): White Plains city, New York |url=http://factfinder2.census.gov/bkmk/table/1.0/en/DEC/10_DP/G001/1600000US3681677 |access-date=January 29, 2013 |publisher=U.S. Census Bureau, American Factfinder}}</ref> According to the city government, the daytime weekday population is estimated at 250,000.<ref>Fernanda Santos, ''New York Times'': [https://www.nytimes.com/2008/01/25/nyregion/25plains.html?fta=y Crimes in White Plains Decline to Record Lows] {{Webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180710133646/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/01/25/nyregion/25plains.html?fta=y |date=July 10, 2018 }}, January 25, 2008.</ref>
